doc.title: Jonathan Scales interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 23, 2025

title: Why 'composer' rather than steel pannist
summary: Scales explains he introduced himself as a composer first because he wrote music before playing pan; the pan is the vehicle.

story.theme_name: Starting the tape: names, dates and places
story.community_name: Interview openings: names, dates and tape setup

blocks.x: I always spend a little time like, all right how am I going to introduce this musician and I decided to use your introduction from your TED talk. And you said to the audience, “I’m a musician, a composer, internationally-touring performer, and band leader. And I was curious, you didn’t say steel pannist.
Was that an oversight or was there a reason for that?

You know I think that maybe that was some type of like a psychological slip but kind of deep at the same time. Because I feel like – I always feel like steel pan happened to be the vehicle that I landed upon. So like as a composer I started writing music when I was like ten years old, and that was before I ever played the steel pan. So I think I resonate more with being a composer and someone who creates music in that way. And I think steel pan happens to be the vehicle that has taken me to where I’ve gotten to. But I think down in the core of myself I always consider myself a composer first and foremost. And I feel like my music sounds like it does on any instrument. You know, like if it’s a string quartet or is it a marimba piece or a wind ensemble piece or an orchestra piece, or I’m writing parts for other people in my band, it sounds like my voice. So I think that maybe it was a little of a philosophical slip but I probably didn’t mean to leave that out.

I was sometimes curious if you went to a cocktail party or something and no one really knew who you were and someone asked you, “So what do you do?” And if you said, “Well I’m a pannist” then of course you’d be forced to explain the whole thing. So maybe “musician” is –
You answered my question really I had in my head and that was you were a musician before you took up the pans. So if you hadn’t taken up the steel pans, what would your instrument be at this point?
